newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BSE to launch options in mid-January. [CORRECTED 11:49 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hungary BSE to launch options in mid-January. [CORRECTED 11:49 GMT]

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) plans to launch its standardised options markets in mid-January 1998 (corrects year from 1997), with the initial contracts to be decided by later by market conditions, BSE CEO Jozsef Rotyis said.
"The preparatory phase of the options markets is concluded," Rotyis told a news conference on Friday. "The planned time to start is mid-January."
Rotyis said Hungary's Central Clearing and Depositary House (Keler) will by that time have an options settlement system and a new futures settlement system as well.

"This system will use portfolio-centred risk management, a first for the Hungarian market," he said, adding that this would result in a reduction of at least 10 percent in the minimum required deposits.

Rotyis said the stock exchange was preparing options contracts for all products, including the BUX index and shares, interest-type contracts and currency contracts, but would decide the initial products up to three months before the launch.
The choice would be made on the basis of market demand and the market's underlying performance, he said.
The CEO said the BSE was planning American-style options for most products but would probably use European options for the shares.
American options can be exercised any time before expiry while European options can only be exercised at expiry.

The BSE launched its standardised futures market in March 1995 and now offers contracts in BUX futures, three- and 12-month discount treasury bills, one- and three-month BUBOR (Budapest Interbank Offered Rate), and the mark, U.S. dollar and Ecu.
